features.name: ProjectViewSet: anonymous clients can read and write projects
features.description: project/views.py get_permissions() never consults permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated, IsEmployee]: list and retrieve get an empty permission list (DRF treats that as no checks at all) and create/update/partial_update get AllowAny. Only destroy and restore require IsEmployee. Actual behaviour is pinned by project/tests/tests_projects.py (test_create_is_open_to_anonymous, test_partial_update_is_open_to_anonymous, test_is_authenticated_is_declared_but_never_applied) - fixing the view will turn those three red on purpose.

features.name: Form-encoded project writes silently set is_active=False
features.description: ProjectSerializer exposes is_active, and DRF sets BooleanField.default_empty_html = False, so for multipart/form bodies a missing boolean is read as False rather than as 'not supplied'. A POST without is_active therefore creates a project that get_queryset() hides from the default list, and a PUT deactivates an existing one; the identical body sent as JSON keeps is_active=True. Pinned by test_create_via_form_data_lands_inactive and test_put_without_is_active_deactivates_project. The same trap applies to any serializer exposing a BooleanField whose model default is True.

features.name: Project restore response nests the project under a 'topic' key
features.description: project/views.py restore() returns {'message': ..., 'topic': serializer.data} - a copy-paste artefact from the topic app. Renaming the key to 'project' is a breaking change for existing clients, so it is recorded rather than corrected. Pinned by test_restore_response_nests_project_under_topic_key.

features.name: Unordered querysets paginated in template_form and working_form
features.description: A full test run emits DRF's UnorderedObjectListWarning for TemplateForm and WorkingForm: their list querysets have no deterministic ordering, so PageNumberPagination can return the same row on two pages and skip another as rows are inserted. Neither model sets Meta.ordering and neither viewset applies an explicit order_by. Project, Question, Topic and TechStack are unaffected - they all declare Meta.ordering. Surfaced while unifying the test layout (QA-6), not covered by any test yet.

features.name: Test suite
features.description: Unit + API tests for services, permissions, cloning logic, WebSocket consumers; coverage reporting. Partially done: question and project viewsets are fully covered and mutation-checked, and the three form stages have soft-delete tests. Still untouched: the three clone_* functions in services.py (highest bug density in the repo), most permission classes, and working_form/consumers.py. See .claude/rules/testing.md for the current baseline.

features.name: Test coverage for the employee app
features.description: employee has no test file at all - zero tests for AUTH_USER_MODEL, the JWT endpoints (register/me/logout/token), CustomUserManager.create_user defaulting is_staff=True, and IsAdminUserOrReadOnly. It is the last app with no coverage.

features.name: Delete leftover startapp test stubs
features.description: employee/tests.py and question/tests/tests.py contained only the generated '# Create your tests here.' comment. An empty stub reads as 'this app has tests' in any file listing and inflated the scaffold-tests preflight inventory. Both deleted; employee now has no test file, which is the honest signal.

features.name: One test layout canon: a tests/ package in every app
features.description: The repo carried two layouts (tests/ package in question, topic, techstack; flat tests.py in template_form, working_form, evaluation_form, project, employee). Unified on the package: <app>/tests/__init__.py plus one file per concern named tests_<plural>.py, moved with git mv so line history survives. Rationale: the cover-first order in .claude/rules/testing.md (services.py, permissions.py, consumers.py) means several test modules per app, which a flat file cannot hold. Updated with it: .claude/rules/testing.md, the scaffold-tests conventions and SKILL example, and the preflight destination check, which now always proposes a package instead of falling back to a flat module.

features.name: Deduplicate the four IsEmployee permission classes
features.description: question, topic, techstack and project each carry a verbatim copy of IsEmployee. Changing one leaves the other three on the old behaviour and no test detects the drift. Note the class is effectively an IsAuthenticated alias: it does an isinstance check against Employee, which is AUTH_USER_MODEL, so every logged-in user passes it.
